A1.justification: These are revisions of the same research work, renamed from LLM-QE to ExpandR. Both PDFs provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices, allowing reliable comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, expansion and reward ablations, query-level analyses and an appendix case study.

after.justification: v3 reports original retrieval and ablation results, alongside additional backbone, Recall@100, transfer and entailment evaluations.

M1.justification: The supervised retriever loss changes from using expansion embeddings alone to averaging original-query and expansion embeddings during training (v1 Eqs. 5–6; v3 Eqs. 8–9). DPO and both reciprocal-rank rewards remain equivalent after renaming. The joint-training framing does not establish an additional iterative training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English E5 training mixture and evaluate MS MARCO and the same 14 BEIR tasks. The additional backbone, transfer and quality analyses use retained data without adding languages, populations or retrieval tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds DPR and ANCE to Table 2 and eight additional comparators in Table 5, including RocketQA, BGE-M3-EN, TAS-B, Gen-Q, ColBERT, E5, WebDRO and Nomic-Embed. v1's PRF and Q2Q/Q2E/Q2C comparisons disappear; document-expansion controls remain in other experiments as vanilla-LLM variants.

E3.justification: The reported retriever learning rate changes from 3e-5 to 1e-5. v3 introduces additional retriever and LLM configurations, fixed-Contriever-reward transfer evaluations, Recall@100, entailment scoring and a ten-pair T-SNE analysis. The principal training sample counts and epoch budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds separate LLM-training and retriever-training ablations across two backbones, embedding visualization, LLM substitution, cross-retriever transfer and entailment analysis. Expansion-format ablations and the Pearson-correlation analysis are removed. The earlier BLEU, expansion-length, 100-query improvement and case-study analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both specify permutation testing at p < 0.05 and mark significant comparisons. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or run-level standard deviations. The retained query-level distribution plots do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive backbone, baseline, Recall@100, transfer and entailment results while removing expansion-format and correlation results. The full Contriever-based model's Avg.All nDCG@10 changes from 47.56 to 47.12 in Table 2; revised training prevents interpreting this as a controlled performance change. Several earlier BLEU, length and case-study values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds a probability factorization, log-likelihood formulation and separate optimization expressions for retriever and LLM parameters (Eqs. 4–7 and 10). This is a limited formal addition beyond v1's operational losses; neither supplies theorems or proofs. The new factorization does not marginalize over possible generated expansions.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on ranking-aligned query expansion, hallucination reduction and improvements with frozen or fine-tuned Contriever. v3 presents the central contribution as joint, mutually adaptive LLM–retriever optimization and end-to-end alignment, with generalization across backbones. This substantially redefines the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets component ablations and embeddings as evidence for complementary joint optimization, and transfer results as evidence against retriever-specific overfitting. It adds entailment-based faithfulness interpretations and joint-training overhead to the limitations. The earlier correlation-based discussion of information benefiting Contriever while misleading BGE is removed.

D1.justification: v3 updates the retriever learning rate and backbone identifiers, removes Q2Q/Q2E/Q2C prompt templates, and changes the advertised code location from LLM-QE to ExpandR. Most data-preparation, LoRA, batch-size, epoch and sampling details persist. The new entailment evaluation does not specify its scorer or scoring procedure.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work shift substantially from traditional query expansion, pseudo-relevance feedback and hallucination mitigation toward LLM supervision and joint retrieval alignment. v3 introduces positioning around works including LLM-QL, DRAMA, RePlug, Syntriever and DeepRetrieval, while removing much of the earlier PRF-focused literature.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology and conclusion are extensively rewritten around joint training. The method and reward terminology change, method subsections are reorganized, and the appendix structure expands and relocates retained analyses. These changes substantially exceed localized editing.

P2.justification: The opening retrieval-pipeline figure is removed and the method diagram becomes a redesigned two-stage illustration. Main comparison and ablation tables are rebuilt, and an embedding figure and several appendix tables are added. Reward plots are split, with length moved to Figure 5 and correlation removed.

improvement.justification: Two-backbone component ablations and cross-retriever transfer strengthen empirical support beyond v1's Contriever-focused evaluation, providing a limited net improvement despite losing expansion-format and correlation analyses. Important weaknesses temper the gains: the new likelihood factorization omits marginalization over expansions (Eq. 4), and the entailment scorer is unspecified (Appendix A.8), limiting the added formal explanation and reproducibility.
